summary: A customer-facing medical triage model uses patient notes and drafts recommendations with no human review.
A recruiting system screens CVs and ranks candidates using third-party cloud inference and stores personal data.
A bank underwriting model is retrained monthly, but there are no documented model cards, lineage records, or decision logs.
A content moderation classifier is deployed across EU markets and can flag users automatically without an appeal path.
A foundation model is exposed through an API without rate limiting, access control, or adversarial testing.
A sales copilot uses internal documents through retrieval augmented generation and logs prompts but has no drift monitoring.
An insurance claims model relies on external vendor data and no DPIA has been performed.
A university admissions assistant provides recommendations and humans can override it, but escalation paths are unclear.
A biometric verification system is planned for public-facing use in EU operations.
An internal compliance assistant generates policy suggestions and stores full prompt and response traces.
An internet-facing portal is exposed to credential stuffing and lacks MFA, rate limiting, and audit logging.
A supply-chain attack could inject malicious packages into the deployment pipeline.
A data lake stores sensitive records without encryption or access segregation.
A phishing campaign targets admins through email and mobile push notification workflows.
A ransomware scenario affects backup restoration, incident response, and recovery drills.
A cloud API lacks input validation and is vulnerable to injection and abusive request volume.
A production container image is pulled from an unsigned registry and has no scanning.
A secrets vault rotation process is missing and credentials are reused across services.
A logging pipeline does not preserve forensic evidence after an incident.
A remote access channel allows third-party vendors to connect without strong authentication.
